title: Villagers attack a balloon
body: When an unmanned hydrogen balloon came down near Gonesse, frightened villagers attacked it with pitchforks.

title: The first people to fly
body: Two men drifted over Paris in a Montgolfier hot-air balloon, watched by huge crowds.

title: Sprouting cows
body: A popular cartoon showed people vaccinated with cowpox growing cows from their bodies. Vaccination went on to wipe out smallpox.

title: The Luddites
body: Textile workers smashed the new machines they said were destroying skilled jobs and wages.

title: The year without a summer
body: After a volcanic eruption in Indonesia, summer frosts ruined harvests across Europe and North America.

title: Cholera arrives
body: Cholera reached Britain and killed tens of thousands. Many blamed foul air rather than dirty water.

title: The Great Moon Hoax
body: The New York Sun reported bat-winged people living on the Moon. Sales soared before the story was exposed.

title: The Great Disappointment
body: Followers of the preacher William Miller expected the world to end on 22 October 1844. Many sold farms and gave away their goods. The day passed quietly.

title: Railway mania
body: British investors piled into hundreds of new railway schemes. Share prices collapsed in 1847, but much of the network got built.

title: The Great Stink
body: A hot summer made the sewage-choked Thames unbearable, even inside Parliament. MPs approved Joseph Bazalgette's sewer system that same summer.

title: A cable under the Atlantic
body: The first transatlantic telegraph messages set off celebrations, and fireworks in New York set City Hall's roof alight. The cable failed within a month.

title: The sky catches fire
body: A huge solar storm lit auroras far into the tropics, and telegraph lines sparked.

title: A voice from a machine
body: At a demonstration of Edison's phonograph in Paris, one academician accused the presenter of ventriloquism.

title: The man with the red flag
body: Britain's 1865 law made road locomotives follow a person on foot carrying a red flag. When it was relaxed in 1896, motorists celebrated with a run to Brighton.

title: Comet pills
body: Astronomers announced that Earth would pass through the tail of Halley's Comet, which contained cyanogen gas. Some people bought "comet pills" and sealed their windows.

title: A new influenza
body: A flu pandemic spread worldwide and killed tens of millions. Masks and closures met resistance.

title: The wireless arrives
body: The BBC began daily radio broadcasts. Within a few years, millions of homes had a licence.

title: Lindbergh lands in Paris
body: After more than 33 hours alone over the Atlantic, Charles Lindbergh landed at Le Bourget to a crowd of tens of thousands.

title: The talkies
body: Audiences cheered The Jazz Singer, the first feature film with synchronised dialogue and song.

title: Black Tuesday
body: Panic selling crashed the New York stock market over a few days in October.

title: Pictures by wireless
body: The BBC opened a regular high-definition television service to a small audience in London.

title: The War of the Worlds
body: Newspapers reported that Orson Welles's radio drama about a Martian invasion caused mass panic. Later research suggests few listeners were fooled.

title: The World of Tomorrow
body: New York's World's Fair showed a future of motorways and gleaming cities in GM's Futurama. Crowds queued for hours as war began in Europe.
